To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the level of local agent cooperation in a small multi-linked cooperative multi-agent system is determined by the degree of distraction in the negotiation process.
the global system performance is determined by a) the degree of local cooperation between the agents and b) the degree of distraction of the agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the local attitude of an agent affects the performance of a system, and how the global performance of the system can be predicted.
understanding and optimizing the performance of a multi-agent system in a dynamic environment.

the model presented in this paper is a significant step towards a better understanding of multi-agent systems.
the model is a good tool for understanding the behaviors of a cooperative multi-agent systems.
this paper provides a clear and complete analysis of the relationship between the degree of local cooperation and global system performance in the context of a cooperative negotiation system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a theoretical foundation for the development of intelligent agents that are capable of dynamic adjustment of their negotiation strategies.

we are able to provide a formal model for the analysis of a cooperative multi-linked negotiation problem, to explain the system behavior in terms of the local and global performance, and to provide design equations for the development of distributed mechanisms that can optimize the system performance dynamically.

the global system performance can be optimized by adjusting the level of local attitude cooperation.
